lesson.subtitle: Ouvir quem defende o quê — e entrar na conversa
lesson.title_tag: Stephanie -- Lesson 02 -- Three People, One Material
lesson.grammar_point: linguagem de checagem e de posicionamento (recurso, nao objeto de estudo)
lesson._phases: As 8 etapas do framework listening-into-interaction, contrato v1. Somam 55: 4+3+4+7+9+7+14+7.

items: The call
Your school is deciding whether to adopt a new coursebook. Three people are on the line and you are the only one from your school.
Where it sits
Nothing is decided today. This is the call where each side says what matters to them.
Your job afterwards
Tell your coordinator who wanted what — and ask the one question nobody asked.

predicao.prompt: Before you hear it: on a call like this, who usually speaks first, and why?
choices: The publisher, because they called the meeting
The person who already uses the material, because everyone wants the practical answer first
The author, because it is their book

predicao.title: Two quick predictions. We will check them against the recording.
items: What will the publisher want to talk about?
What will the teacher who already uses it want to talk about?

call1.title: Listen once, for the big picture
turnos: Thanks for joining, everyone. I am Tom Reis, from the publisher. The idea today is not to decide anything — it is to hear what each of you needs from a coursebook before we go further.
Marta Bueno. I coordinate at a school that has been using the book for two terms, so I am the one who has actually taught from it.
And Priya Nair. I wrote the second half of it, so I will be honest about what it does badly as well as what it does well.
From my side, the question is the pacing. On paper each unit is ninety minutes. In a real room it is closer to two hours, and that is with a group that talks.
That is useful. What we hear most from schools is the opposite — that there is not enough material for the hour.
That depends entirely on whether the teacher runs the speaking task properly. If they skip it, yes, the unit is short.
The pacing was the part we argued about most. We chose to leave the speaking task long, because cutting it turns the unit into a grammar page. But I understand that it costs the teacher time.
So, to be clear before we go on — Marta, you are saying the material works, and the problem is the clock?
I am saying the material works and the clock has to be planned for. Those are different things, and I would not want the second one written down as a complaint.

gist_call.prompt: What is this call actually for?
choices: To decide whether the school adopts the book
To hear what each side needs, before anything is decided
To fix the pacing problem in the material

quem_quer.title: Listen again. Who wants what?
defs: Wants the design decision understood, not just the complaint
Wants the pacing planned for, and not recorded as a complaint
Wants to know what schools need before going further

items: Marta says the material does not work.
f
She says it works — and that the clock has to be planned for. She corrects Tom on exactly this at the end.
Tom hears the opposite complaint from most schools.
t
He says most schools tell him there is not enough material for the hour.
Priya defends the long speaking task as a choice, not an oversight.
t
She says cutting it would turn the unit into a grammar page — and admits it costs the teacher time.

micro_sort.title: Six lines from the call. Sort each one by what the speaker is doing.
cols: Checking what the other person means
Conceding a point without dropping it
items: So, to be clear before we go on — you are saying the material works?
I am saying the material works and the clock has to be planned for.
I understand that it costs the teacher time.
Those are different things, and I would not want the second one written down as a complaint.
That is useful. What we hear most from schools is the opposite.
What we hear most from schools is that there is not enough material — is that not your experience?

micro_answer.title: Each move, and the line that shows it
items: Checking buys you the right to be wrong.
Tom: “So, to be clear before we go on — you are saying the material works?”
Correcting is not disagreeing.
Marta: “I am saying the material works and the clock has to be planned for.”
Conceding keeps the point alive.
Priya: “But I understand that it costs the teacher time.” — said while keeping the design decision.

prep.label: Take these in. Keywords, not sentences.
items: So, to be clear before we go on…
I am saying…
I understand that…
Those are different things
Can I check one thing before we move on?

prep_frames.title: Say them once, in thought groups, before you need them
items: A

before we move on?
strong
Can I check one thing before we move on?
B

that the pacing is the issue, not the book.
soft

Your side
You join the same call, for your school. You have two minutes: say where your school stands on the pacing, check one thing you did not catch, and ask the question nobody asked.
Their side
Your teacher plays Tom. He will summarise what you said — and he will get one part of it slightly wrong, on purpose.

roleplay.title: Three things have to happen
items: You say where your school stands, without turning it into a complaint.
You check something you did not catch — before it goes in the minutes.
When he summarises you wrongly, you correct how you were understood, not him.

replay.title: Say only the part your teacher marked — once more.
items: Same content. What changes is whether he can answer you.

fecho.title: What we built today
items: Check before it goes in the minutes — being corrected now is cheaper than later.
Correct how you were understood, not the person who understood you.
Agreeing with the cost is not agreeing to change it.

fecho.title: What we worked on today
items: Following three voices on a call, without a transcript
Hearing who wants what, not just what was said
Checking something before it goes in the minutes
Correcting how you were understood, without contradicting the person

fecho.title: How confident do you feel right now?
fecho.sub: Your own reading, today. There is no right answer here.
items: Following a call with three people I do not know
Asking someone to repeat, without losing the thread
Saying where my school stands, in one sentence
Correcting a summary of what I said

fecho.label: Before the next real one
items: The next call or meeting you will join, and roughly when
Check one thing before it goes in the minutes
If they summarise you wrongly, say what you are saying — not that they are wrong
